1.why: MFA routes go through authenticated(), bind actions to auth.session.userId/auth.user, and reject body userId/accountId, so only the signed-in owner can access their MFA settings.

2.why: Identity codes are HMAC-bound to the session id and stored as a per-session hash; TOTP/backup material is per-user, so the same code does not work for arbitrary other users.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/mfa/verify only sets mfaEnabled and backup hashes on the user and does not invalidate other existing sessions in the sessions Map.

4.why: TOTP secret is stored via encrypt() (AES-GCM); backup codes are stored only as peppered SHA-256 hashes in backupHashes.

5.why: Tokens, TOTP seeds, backup codes, encryption key, and pepper all use crypto.getRandomValues (Web Crypto CSPRNG).

6.why: Session id is only in an HttpOnly cookie; client script does not write secrets/OTPs/tokens to localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validates email, phone, password, OTP, and backup input with dedicated validators before use.

8.why: API returns JSON; DOM updates use textContent for secrets/codes and fixed HTML templates, with a strict nonce CSP blocking inline script injection.

9.why: Sign-in only accepts destination === "/"; other redirects are the fixed HTTP→HTTPS localhost upgrade, not open user-controlled URLs.

10.why: hdr() sets CSP (including frame-ancestors 'none'), HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, and X-Frame-Options: DENY on responses.

11.why: sessionCookie sets mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict.

12.why: Generic fail messages and no server logging of secrets; tokens/codes are not placed in URLs; user-facing errors omit stack traces.

13.why: Identity and pending TOTP codes have LIFE expiry and single-use flags; TOTP counters are consumed via accepted; backup codes are removed from the hash set after use.

14.why: Identity, TOTP, and backup paths increment failure counters and lock for LOCK after MAX failed attempts.

15.why: rotate() issues a new session id on sign-in/identity auth; active() enforces idle and absolute timeouts; logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
